newsitem.title: FRANCE: Court bars wildcat strikes at Air France Europe.
newsitem.headline: Court bars wildcat strikes at Air France Europe.

text.p: A Paris court has ruled that Air France Europe unions may no longer stage wildcat strikes and must give management at least five days' notice.
But it did not rule against the unions in an action brought by Air France after a disruptive strike that ended on Saturday, the day of the ruling.
The unions have called a string of snap strikes to protest against the conditions of a merger between the regional airline Air France Europe and the international carrier Air France.
Employees at Air France Europe, formerly Air Inter, have traditionally received better pay and benefits than their colleagues at Air France.
A spokeswoman for Air France Europe said the ruling was not a victory for either the airline or the unions.

The court upheld Air France's argument that Air France Europe's unions are bound by the same five-day strike warning requirement as the unions at Air France since April 1, the day Air France formally began to manage Air France Europe.
The Communist-led CGT union said in a statement that 11,000 Air France Europe employees are now part of Air France and urged rapid elections for new union representatives.
